paragraphs: Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef. When he came, he said: a case occurred before R. Yoḥanan, in the synagogue of Ma'on, on Yom Kippur that fell on Shabbat, etc.; Abaye relied on it, etc. They objected: did he not himself say, 'Avin is reliable'? That is, one may rely on what Avin says in R. Yoḥanan's name; Yitzḥak Sumka is not reliable, because Avin is constantly before R. Yoḥanan. If R. Yoḥanan retracts something he said initially, Ravin hears and retracts too; but Rav Yitzḥak is not constantly before him to know whether he retracted, chapter HaBa Al Yevimto (64b). Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef used to inquire through dealings with demons, and the demon sought to harm him. (A miracle was performed for him—Rashi.) He was swallowed in a cedar, and a miracle was performed for him: the cedar split, Ḥelek (101a). Rashi's wording suggests that the miracle was the cedar's swallowing him, while the Gemara's wording implies that the miracle was the cedar's splitting. In the West they said: Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef said, Shabbat, chapter 1 (13b). When he came, he said: when the prayer leader finished the sounding in Yavneh, a person could not hear his own ears, Rosh HaShanah (30a). He had money owed to him by R. Abba's household; he came before R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa, Bava Batra (170, end of side a). R. Abbahu sent him to bring wine from the Samaritans' house. He found that old man (Tosafot cites an interpretation identifying him as Elijah, etc.). He went and told R. Abbahu, and R. Abbahu told R. Ammi and R. Assi; they did not move until they had made them full gentiles, Ḥullin, chapter 1 (6a). (See Rashba [רשב״א, unexpanded here].) He found R. Abbahu standing among the people of Usha, etc.; he learned it from him forty times, Pesaḥim (72a), Ketubbot (50a). In Pesaḥim there, 'de-inshei' is a scribal error and should read 'de-Usha.' He visited Abaye's house on a festival, saw him recite a blessing over each and every cup, and said to him, 'Does the master not accept this statement of R. Yehoshua ben Levi?' Berakhot (42b); see above. When he came, he said that R. Aḥa bar Ḥanina’s [statement] was not stated explicitly [the cited Bavli has no separate R.A.], Berakhot (9a). R. Ammi (see above). R. Assi (see above). Rav Huna (see his entry). Before R. Ḥanina bar Pappi. He came from Cappadocia to Lod and encountered Rav Yehudah, Zohar, Midrash HaNe'elam, Toledot, section Vaye'tar. R. Yehudah son of R. Shimon (see below). He said, 'R. Yoḥanan said,' Kirah (45b, 58a), chapter Ḥavit (147a), Eruvin (22, end of side a), Ta'anit (10a), Yevamot (104a), Sanhedrin (4a), Ḥullin (43a), several statements. R. Yitzḥak son of R. Yose said: R. Yoḥanan said, Niddah (65b) and Temurah (26a). In Tosafot there: bar Yosef; and afterward in Tosafot, bar Yose should read Yosef. He said, 'R. Yannai said,' Ḥullin (105a), Nazir (42b). R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa (see above). He followed R. Yirmeyah in the butchers' market, saw [lungs] standing with growths upon growths, and said to him, 'Does the master not want pieces of meat?' (He wished to know whether he would declare them fit.) He said to him: when such a case came before R. Yoḥanan, he would send it before R. Yehudah son of R. Shimon, who ruled permissively, though he himself did not accept that view, chapter Ellu Terefot (48a). R. Yirmeyah called him and Rav Huna ‘children’ (see his entry). Rav Yitzḥak bar Yose (it should read Yosef), Ravin, and Abaye visited Rav Pappi's house, Ḥullin (110a). When he came, he said: all the mezuzot in Rabbi's house, Menaḥot (33a). And Ravin (see above). Yuḥasin writes: Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef [spoke] to Rava (I did not find that he spoke to Rava). He writes: perhaps Rav Dimi bar Yosef is his brother (see his entry).
